title: Donât Put Yourself a Box
description:
Photo by Piotr MusioÅ / Unsplash

Donât Put Yourself in a Box

Personal Development and Career Growth

  • Apr 26, 2024

Summary

  • Companies need "boxes" (job classifications) to grow and function. This makes hiring, compensation, and career development tractable, and promotes fair treatment of employees.
  • If the boxes are too large, a company can't grow. If the boxes are too small, innovation and ownership are smothered.
  • The size of a company's boxes is directly proportional to the level of trust employees have for management.
  • To get hired, put yourself in the box the company is hiring for. Tailor your resume to highlight those skills and experiences; put yourself out there as a âspecialistâ in the thing theyâre hiring for.
  • If aiming for a promotion, demonstrate how your work embodies the behaviors and impacts of the next-level âboxâ.
  • Don't let those boxes define you. Your value and identity goes far beyond any job description.

Hot Take

Businesses can't function at scale unless they put people in standardized "boxes"; if you want to be hired and to grow your career, you need to understand that, and understand how to work with those boxes. On the other hand, you can't be reduced to a box, and if you tie your identity to those boxes in your thinking, you'll limit yourself in ways that are unnatural and harmful.

This is like the paradox of SchrÃ¶dinger's Cat, both alive and dead at the same time. Like with quantum mechanics and the cat, whether youâre in a box or not depends on whoâs doing the measuring: your employer, or you.

My Box Origin Story

My introduction to the idea of âboxesâ came in the late 2000s, when I noticed that people at Google were having a hard time getting hired or promoted if they were doing âoperationalâ work that didnât involve much traditional program management. Whether they were being considered for hiring or promotion, they were told, essentially, âYouâve done some great work, but itâs not program management; weâre not sure what role/ladder is a fit for you, but itâs not this one. Next!â

This was clearly a problemâeven though they didnât do PERT diagrams and Gantt charts, Googlers did important work in these roles, and roadblocks to hiring and promoting them created both operational and retention issues as jobs went vacant and high-performing employees felt their value wasnât being recognized. As a member of both Program Management hiring and promotion committees at Google I had more visibility to this issue than most others; I spoke to a friend of mine in People Operations (Googleâs HR), who turned out to already be well aware of this problem from repeatedly dealing with upset hiring managers and frustrated promotion candidates. Together, we hatched a plan: to create a new job ladder (job classification) for these âoperationalâ program managers to move to, that was better suited to the type of work they did.

We gathered some data, wrote a proposal, and set up a meeting with the SVP responsible for all engineering at Google. The SVP had been in quite a few meetings Iâd presented to before; I knew him to be not only a brilliant and capable leader, but a genuinely nice guy, too, so I had no worries about the meeting. Imagine my shock then, when this âgenuinely nice guyâ started yelling at us, telling my partner and I that we were going to wreck Google culture!

I vividly remember what he said: âDONâT PUT PEOPLE IN BOXES!â He told us Google needed some job classifications, but that our culture required those classifications to be both broad and vague so both employees and their managers wouldnât be blocked from doing whatever needed to be done. The worst thing we could do, the SVP told us, was to make the classification âboxesâ so small people could say âthatâs not my jobââwhich is precisely what he saw us proposing to do!

A year or two before this Google had shifted from having just three job types (over-broadly, they were âengineersâ, âtechnical people that donât do engineeringâ, and âeveryone elseâ) to having around around a dozen (one of which was my ladder, âTechnical Program Managersâ). There had been a lot of debate about whether those boxes were already too smallâ¦ but the senior team had decided 12â15 job categories were acceptableâenough large boxes to make hiring, career development, and compensation more efficient, but not so many that jobs were defined too narrowly. We left his office dejected, but also enlightened: it said a lot to me that this SVP thought it so important to Googleâs culture, a lesson Iâve never forgotten. (Times have changed though; Google now has many more job ladders, including at least 5â10 âoperationalâ ladders broken off from Program Management well beyond what my friend and I had proposed).

Why Companies Need Boxes

Why do we need âboxesâ (job classifications) at all? Wouldnât the world be better if everyone just did whatever they saw that needed doing? The value of boxes to corporations comes down to two things: scaling and trust.

Scaling

If youâre in a small startup, you want employees who can wear many hats, and who wonât feel limited by things like job titles. Because there are so few employees, and because you know everyone personally and need everyone you hire to have an outsized impact, you can afford to put a lot of energy into every individual hiring decision. Compensation planning is pretty lightweight and customized, both because there arenât many people to deal with, and because you want to compensate people based on their contribution to the business, regardless of what their title is. Everyone is a âspecial snowflakeâ.

That changes quickly as your startup growsâyou cross a line where it becomes infeasible to treat every hire as a unique individual, with bespoke hiring and compensation. This is where âboxesâ become necessary: you have to put people into categories, with standards for how hiring, compensation, and career progression work for each boxâitâs the only way you can scale the company. The alternative to this would be to allow an increasing number of managers to continue bespoke hiring and comp within their own areasâ¦ which leads to the second issue, trust.

Trust

Because startups are so risky, the ability of potential employees to trust the founders is a big dealâif they donât appear trustworthy, theyâre not going to attract the kind of people they need. As the company grows, the number of managers that both employees and senior management need to trust grows, too. At some point it becomes too much: employeesâ willingness to âhave faithâ that managers will make fair and appropriate decisions drops lower and lower, so much so that everything will fall apart without the enforced fairness of standardized boxes.

ð¡

The size of the boxes in a company are directly proportional to the amount of trust employees have in management

Labor unions are the endgame for this sort of trust problem. One of the big rallying points for companies trying to avoid unionization is always to try to convince employees that management has their best interests at heart, and can be trusted. As a rule, unions have close to zero trust for management, andâas a direct consequenceâunions often push for the smallest âboxesâ possible: boxes for very narrow roles, subdivided by seniority, and sometimes further subdivided by location. They see this as the best way to ensure fairness in an environment where management canât be trusted at all. This is the ultimate version of the cultural harm my SVP was worried about.

Boxes and Hiring

Scaling and trust drive companies to put employees into standard categories, or boxes. How do those boxes affect hiring, and, understanding this, how can you better âsellâ yourself as a candidate for jobs?

Most companies above startup size need to hire for boxes, for the reasons given above; itâs just too much work to do anything else. It would be wonderful if recruiters, interviewers, and hiring managers had the time to carefully read and savor every resume that came in, and then spend time meeting with every candidate to pull out nuances that didnât come across clearly in their job histories. Thatâs not the world we live in, though; there are too many candidates to get through, and too few hours in the day.

The usual practice is for recruiters to work with hiring managers to identify standard requirements (boxes, again!) that can be used to screen out people and reduce the number of candidates they need to go into more depth with (hiring managers will usually never see any of those dropped candidates). Those standard requirements are typically based on a template used for all jobs of the same ladder and level, extended with custom specs tailored to the particular role being hired for. In the language Iâve been using in this article, the job requirements are a very clear âboxâ, and the screening process only lets through candidates whose âshapesâ fit that box, like a childâs sorting toy.

Source: Flickr user rosipaw, CC BY-NC-SA 2.0

When there are lots of candidates for a tiny number of jobs, the recruiters donât magically get more time to handle the extra candidatesâinstead, they often deal with the overload by tightening the screening criteria even further: that is, by making the boxes smaller.

Behaviorally, the shift from âstartupâ to âbig companyâ, and the shift from rapid growth to slow growth, show up to candidates as employers become increasingly selective. Startups like generalists; big companies like specialists. If there are few people vying for each job, hiring managers won't care as much about past experience; if there are many candidates, theyâll only be interested in people whoâve previously done the same kind job theyâre hiring for. These trends are amplified when business is tough and hiring budgets are thin: hiring managers become nervous about using their scarce headcount on unproven candidatesâthey need people who have already shown success in exactly the job the manager needs done.

ð¡

Iâm writing this in April, 2024, in a time of high interest rates and widespread layoffs in tech, and when there are lots of AI-based screening tools being offered that promise to save recruiters time; you do the math about the current hiring marketâ¦

Besides being lucky, there are two powerful ways to cut through âsmall box screeningâ:

  • Put yourself in the box theyâre hiring for. This means customizing your resume for each job you apply for, or at least for each type of job youâre going after. If theyâre hiring for someone with experience doing X, focus your resume on how youâve been successful doing X (or at least, things like X) in the past. When a recruiter or hiring manager looks at your resume, you want them to jump out of their chair and exclaim: âwow, this person is exactly what weâve been looking for!â
  • Pull a Kobayashi Maru by bypassing the whole screening process: use your network of personal connections to get an introduction to the hiring manager. This is probably the single most powerful thing you can do because it exposes you to the hiring manager as a whole person, instead of a peg that fits in a box.

Boxes and Promotions

A similar situation arises with promotions: the people making decisions about whether you should be promoted or not donât (usually) have the familiarity with you, or the time, to make a customized decisionâ¦ and doing so would create fairness issues. Instead, they look at whether you fit the next-level box. I want to talk about two parts to this: one related to the job ladder, and one related to the level.

Job Ladder

I vividly remember one promotion committee I served on, where we were deciding whether or not to promote an individual who had unquestionably performed at the next levelâ¦ but the work theyâd done wasnât consistent with the job ladder (work classification) they were assigned to. They had delivered amazing business impact through striking personal initiative, leadership, and hard workâ¦ but what theyâd done had nothing in common with the sort of work expected for the job ladder, or âboxâ, they were in. Should we promote them, or not? We debated the question for far longer than weâd spent on any other candidate weâd reviewed, called in HR support to advise us, andâ¦ we couldnât decide. The rules were that âif you canât decide, the decision needs to be ânoââ, so we ended by turning down the promotion and recommending the person for a large cash bonus, instead. Our decision was appealed, and the appeal was denied, too, for the same reason: despite the great work, the candidateâs work was outside the box.

Sometimes the process and people deciding on your promotions will be more amenable to âoutside the boxâ work, but really, regardless of whoâs making the promotion decision, and what their ârules of engagementâ are, your chances of success will be greatly enhanced by you being aware of the box imposed by your job ladder as you go about your work, and as you explain that work to others. To be clear: Iâm not saying to limit what you work onâthatâs the ânot my jobâ problem the SVP at the beginning of the article was talking about! What I am saying is that you should proactively plan how you will describe your work in ways consistent with the box.

For example, if youâre a Program Manager and spent a lot of time creating product requirements (the work of a Product Manager at most companies), when you and your direct manager describe it to others, be sure you both talk about (for example) the work you did to understand what other work was dependent on having the requirements, how you delegated and tracked some of the work on market research, bringing it all together into a single document, how you built consensus on the requirements, communicated them to the engineering team, and then managed scope creepâall things that are part of the description of the Program Management box. This makes it easy for the people who will decide on your promotion to say âHuzzah! They did both the Program and Product Managementâ, instead of saying âThis was great Product Management, too bad theyâre a Program Manager.â

Job Level

Really, this is a topic that deserves (and will get) an article all on its own, but I think itâs relevant to surface it here: in general, higher level jobs arenât just harder/bigger/broader versions of lower level jobs: theyâre different âboxesâ altogether. The next-level behaviors senior people are looking for are often behaviors that arenât exercised much, if at all, at your current level. I think of these as âphase changesâ, analogous to the phase changes water goes through as it turns from solid ice to liquid to gas as you turn up the heat: itâs always the same water, but it looks and behaves differently in each phase. Some of these transitions are more abrupt and noticeable than others, but theyâre definitely there. At Google for example, there are noticeable differences between all levels, but the âphase changesâ are especially acute between levels 5 and 6, and between levels 7 and 8.

The takeaway here is that you can greatly increases your chances of success by understanding what those âphase changesâ are (more senior mentors can be super helpful in this)âwhatâs qualitatively different about the next-level boxâand then work with your manager to proactively plan how you will describe your work in ways that highlight those qualitative differences.

Boxes and You

So after telling you about the importance of âboxesâ, now Iâm going to tell youâ¦ to avoid them!

This sure looks like a paradox, but let me explain!

Weâve been talking about how companies, managers, and recruiters use boxes, and how, because of scaling and trust, itâs just not practical for them to operate in any other way. Weâd hope that they donât make the boxes too small, and that they have good judgment in how they apply themâ¦ but boxes are a fact of life in the world of work.

The place where you should avoid boxes isnât in the workplace, though: it's in your head. Itâs completely natural for peopleâs occupation and organization to become a part of their identityâ¦ but it's harmful to let that go too far: you are not your job, and you are not your job title.

A lot has been written about the psychology of tying oneâs identity to their job, but the thing I want to focus on here is how putting yourself in a box in your own thinking (e.g. seeing yourself as a âProduct Managerâ, as a âGooglerâ, and so on) can mean putting counterproductive limits on your own behavior, and your own thinking about whatâs possible.

ð¡

Youâre much more than, and much more capable than, the box youâre in.

From a career perspective, itâs a good practice to periodically take some time out and take stock of where you are now and how that fits with where you want to go. If you do this sort of self-assessment youâll often decide youâre basically on the right path and just need to make some minor adjustmentsâ¦ but sometimes youâll realize that the path youâre on wonât take you where you want to be, and that bigger changes are needed: maybe you should ask your manager for different responsibilities? Change teams? Change job ladders? Even change companies? All of those require seeing beyond the box youâre in.

Even though you need to describe yourself in terms of boxes to get where you are now, if your own thinking is constrained by those boxes, it will be hard for you to see that maybe the best path for you is quite different from the one youâre on. Maybe you should change teams? Roles? Departments? Even change your city, or your employer? Donât get me wrong: I know plenty of people whoâve been in more or less the same job, in the same place, working for the same company, for many years, and theyâre very happyâ¦ but itâs also common for people stay in the same role because they see that role defining them, instead of just being something they do.

How You Can Bring Order From Chaos, Today

Here are some things you can do now to apply these ideas:

  • If youâre looking for a job now, describe yourself as being well inside the box your potential employer is hiring for: tune your resume to the job youâre going after. You should have a different resume at least for every âclassâ of job, and sometimes for each specific job. It can be hard to do it if youâre going after several types of job at the same time, but your LinkedIn resume needs to support the more focused, specialized resumes youâre using. Make sure you highlight the skills and expertise called out in the job ads youâre applying to, and talk about your skill and experience in that area. No one hires generalists, so donât call yourself one in your resume; instead, describe yourself as a specialist in the very thing your target company is hiring for.
  • If youâre working toward a promotion now, put yourself in the box you want to be promoted to. Ask your manager and mentors to help you understand the heart of the next-level box, and think about how you can describe your work, behavior, and accomplishments in terms of that box.
  • Donât tie your identity to the box youâre in. You are a complete person with a personality, skills, and experience that transcend any mere box, and if you tie up your identity with the boxes other people put you in, you will limit the paths you can take and the things you can accomplish.

What Do You Think?

I'd love to hear about your experiences with boxes! If you're a paid supporter of this newsletter (hint, hint!) you can add comments below.

description:
We are looking for a detail-oriented Procurement Specialist to join our team in New York, New York in a contract capacity with the potential for a permanent role. This position will play an important role in supporting day-to-day purchasing operations, maintaining strong vendor documentation, and helping ensure procurement activities run smoothly across the business. The ideal candidate brings sound judgment, strong organizational skills, and the ability to coordinate effectively with suppliers, finance partners, and internal stakeholders in a fast-moving environment.

Responsibilities:
â¢ Manage the full processing cycle for purchase requests and purchase orders, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and timely execution.
â¢ Gather and evaluate vendor quotations for routine buying needs, helping identify competitive pricing and suitable supplier options.
â¢ Assist with supplier setup by collecting and organizing required forms, compliance records, insurance documents, and payment information.
â¢ Maintain current procurement records, including vendor profiles, contract files, and supporting purchasing documentation.
â¢ Monitor open orders, shipment timelines, and invoice-related issues, following up to resolve discrepancies efficiently.
â¢ Partner with Accounts Payable, Finance, and internal teams to address mismatches involving purchase orders, receipts, and invoices.
â¢ Track supplier agreement milestones and renewal timelines while helping maintain an organized contract and vendor calendar.
â¢ Prepare spend reports and purchasing analysis by supplier, category, and department to support business decision-making.
â¢ Help enforce procurement procedures by confirming purchases follow established approval steps and company policy requirements.
â¢ Contribute to sourcing activities by supporting bid reviews, supplier comparisons, reporting needs, audit documentation, and process improvement efforts within procurement systems and records management.
â¢ Bachelorâs degree in business, supply chain, accounting, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
â¢ 1â3 years of experience in procurement, purchasing, accounts payable, vendor administration, or a related function.
â¢ Working knowledge of corporate procurement practices, purchase order processing, and buying workflows.
â¢ Exposure to vendor support activities, contract-related administration, or contract negotiation coordination is preferred.
â¢ Strong Excel skills and experience using purchasing platforms or enterprise procurement systems.
â¢ Excellent attention to detail with the ability to manage documentation, deadlines, and multiple priorities effectively.
â¢ Clear communication and sound problem-solving skills for working with suppliers and cross-functional internal teams.
â¢ Ability to perform well in a fast-paced environment that requires adaptability and strong follow-through.

title: Senior Platform Engineer - Kafka (d/f/m)
Design Engineer
description:
Mercura (YC W25) helps the companies that build the real world move at software speed, automating the back-office work that runs the $12 trillion industry behind every hospital, school, and power plant. We started with one of their biggest bottlenecks - turning messy technical requests into accurate quotes - and grew to $2M ARR in our first year. With a team of 16, we're now targeting $10M by the end of 2026 as well as our expansion into the US.

About the role

We're hiring our first Design Engineer to own the look, feel, and implementation of our product. You'll work closely with our CPO and engineers to design clean, intuitive interfaces for non-technical users and ship them to production yourself. In this role, you will bridge design and engineering end-to-end - speaking directly to customers, turning insight into interfaces, and building them with code.

What you will be working on

  • Talk directly to customers, understand their problems, and translate findings into clean product requirements and interface designs

  • Build prototypes with AI tools and in code to test product hypotheses with customers fast

  • Create and implement intuitive, AI-first interfaces that make complex B2B workflows effortless

  • Own the full journey from design to production - working closely with engineers to ship new features

What we're looking for

  • You have 2-5 years of experience as a design engineer, product designer, or frontend engineer with a strong portfolio in AI & complex B2B SaaS products

  • You love speaking to customers directly to identify pain points and problems

  • You are highly proficient in AI-tools (Lovable, Cursor, Claude, ...) and Figma to design and prototype fast

  • You are comfortable shipping code (React, Typescript, Python) to production - this is as much an engineering role as it is a design role

  • You are comfortable working in a fast-paced startup environment and want to build something from the ground up

  • You want to work in-person from our Munich office or are willing to relocate

  • Fluent in German and English (our users are mostly German-speaking only)

About the Founders

We are Lukas, Stefan & Sean, the co-founders of Mercura.

We share a deep commitment to excellence and the discipline to pursue what others might consider impossible.

Two of us come from non-academic families, and we all know what it means to create our own paths and overcome barriers. This experience shapes our belief in equal opportunity and fuels our dedication to social mobility.

Lukas (left) is responsible for business development at Mercura. With his background as a Data Scientist at Allianz and at Google in Silicon Valley, he brings extensive expertise in data and AI.
Lukas’ family has been active in the construction industry for over 100 years, giving him a deep understanding and passion for the sector's specific needs.

Sean (middle) is responsible for technical development at Mercura. As a top 0.01% physicist, Sean earned a Silver medal for Germany at the International Physics Olympiad (IPhO), began researching with the Max Planck Institute at the age of 16, and has since published at leading machine learning conferences.

Stefan (right) leads product development at Mercura. Previously, he worked in management consulting at Bain & Company, where he helped manufacturers improve their operations.
Stefan leverages his research experience at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and Harvard Business School to develop innovative solutions for the industry.

At Mercura, we believe that the best ideas emerge when people from different backgrounds collaborate together. We hire based on ability, mindset, and values, and we live by one simple rule: the best idea wins.

Beyond Mercura, we actively support initiatives that promote diversity and gender equity and commit a portion of our personal income each year to organizations expanding opportunity for others.

 

Our company values

Customer first. We stay close to our customer’s reality and use their feedback to build what truly matters and earn their lasting trust.

Ownership. We take responsibility end-to-end and act proactively to pursue the most ambitious goals.

Enjoy the ride. We build a culture where people can be themselves, have fun doing meaningful work, and celebrate wins along the way.

Let the best ideas win. We challenge each other respectfully and judge ideas by merit, not who said it.

Down-to-earth. We are approachable, humble, and hands-on, bringing both heart and mind to everything we do.

  • Entwicklung eines besseren Verständnisses für Patient:innen Bedürfnisse, Verhalten und Customer Journeys

Commercial & Analytics

title: (Senior) Customer Success Manager (alle Geschlechter)
description:
Deine High-Speed Mission

Zu Speed Kit

Speed Kit macht die Shops und Websites unserer Kunden messbar schneller, und schnellere Seiten heißen mehr Umsatz. Zu unseren Kunden gehören einige der bekanntesten E-Commerce-Marken in Deutschland und Europa.

Zu deiner Rolle

Customer Success bei uns ist deshalb keine Zufriedenheitsverwaltung, sondern die Verantwortung dafür, dass ein Kunde live geht, den Effekt auf sein Geschäft nachvollziehen kann und langfristig bleibt. Die initiale Unterschrift holen unsere Account Executives. Danach sitzt du im Driver Seat: Du bringst den Kunden durch Trial oder POC über die Ziellinie und behältst ihn anschließend in deinem Portfolio. Der Kunde bleibt deiner, mit allem was dazugehört.

Was du verantwortest

  • Du führst Trials und POCs deiner Neukunden: Du steuerst Integration und Konfiguration mit unserem Team und dem Kunden, koordinierst A/B-Test-Setup und Auswertung und hältst die Stakeholder zusammen. Du erkennst früh, wenn ein Projekt kippt, und drehst es. 

  • Du führst die Onboarding-Projekte als echte Projektleitung, von Kickoff über Go-live bis zur Ergebnispräsentation. Das ist der Schwerpunkt der Rolle.

  • Du betreust deine Bestandskunden aus eigenem Antrieb. Du gehst auf deine Accounts zu, bevor sie sich melden, kennst ihre Roadmap und ihre Relaunches und bringst regelmäßig Ergebnisse und Ideen an den Tisch.

  • Du trägst Umsatzverantwortung für dein Portfolio: Verlängerungen, Commitment-Upgrades, Überschreitungen, Ausbau in weitere Domains, Marken und Länder. Du weißt jederzeit, wo dein Book steht und warum. Und weil dein Erfolg unser Erfolg ist, profitierst du auch entsprechend davon.

  • Du führst Kundengespräche auf Basis von Daten: Core Web Vitals, CrUX, Conversion-Uplift, ROI. Du kannst einen Uplift erklären und auch eine Verschlechterung, ohne auszuweichen.

  • Du arbeitest täglich mit AI. Analysen, Reporting, Datenrecherche über unsere Systeme, Entwürfe für Kundenkommunikation: das machst du mit Claude und Gemini und baust dir eigene wiederverwendbare Workflows dafür. Wir erwarten kein Coding, aber wir erwarten, dass du dir selbst Hebel baust, statt Dinge manuell abzuarbeiten.

  • Du bist die Spinne im Netz. Niemand im Unternehmen weiß so viel über unsere Kunden wie du, und du bringst dieses Wissen in alle Teams, von Engineering und Product über Sales bis zur Geschäftsführung.


Wie es bei uns wirklich läuft

Das Customer Success Team ist eine kleine, extrem eingespielte Truppe und liefert unseren Kunden echten, messbaren Mehrwert. Das ist eine High-Impact-Rolle: Was du bewegst, ist sofort sichtbar, im Ergebnis des Kunden und in unseren Zahlen. Dazu extrem flache Hierarchien, kein Freigabetheater, direkte Gespräche mit Engineering, Product und Geschäftsführung. Was du entscheidest, gilt. Dafür brauchst du aber auch eine eigene Meinung und den Mut, sie auszusprechen. Wenn du etwas anders siehst, sagst du es, und du bleibst dabei, auch wenn jemand widerspricht.

Wir haben mehr Projekte als Hände. Ein Teil deiner Woche wird von außen bestimmt, deshalb ist gute Triage entscheidend: Du erkennst, welches der zehn offenen Themen heute Umsatz bewegt oder einen Kunden hält, und was warten kann. Du bekommst von uns Ziele, Kontext und Rückendeckung, aber niemand sortiert deine Prioritäten für dich. Dazu gehört auch, dass du den Mund aufmachst, wenn es brennt: nicht bei jeder Unsicherheit, sondern nachdem du selbst ernsthaft versucht hast, das Problem zu lösen. Keine Probleme, die drei Wochen im Stillen wachsen, und keine Eskalation für jede Frage, die du selbst beantworten könntest.


Dein Ticket für unser Raumschiff

  • Mindestens 2 Jahre Customer Success oder Account Management im B2B SaaS

  • Erfahrung in der Steuerung technischer Onboarding-, Trial- oder Implementierungsprojekte mit mehreren Stakeholdern auf Kundenseite

  • Erfahrung mit oder klare Bereitschaft zu echter Umsatzverantwortung. Du willst, dass dein Ergebnis an Kundenerfolg hängt, statt es zu vermeiden.

  • AI-Tools als tägliches Arbeitsmittel. Das ist harte Voraussetzung und kein Pluspunkt. Wir werden dich im Bewerbungsprozess bitten, konkret zu zeigen, was du mit Claude, Gemini oder vergleichbaren Tools gebaut oder automatisiert hast. "Ich nutze ChatGPT manchmal für E-Mails" reicht dafür nicht.

  • Selbstbewusstsein und Standing. Du trittst gegenüber Entscheidern auf Augenhöhe auf, führst auch unangenehme Gespräche über Preise, Verzögerungen und Erwartungen, und widersprichst einem Kunden freundlich, wenn er falsch liegt.

  • Digitale Tools sind für dich selbstverständlich. Ein neues System bringst du dir selbst bei, statt auf eine Schulung zu warten.

  • Ausgeprägte Eigenständigkeit und saubere Priorisierung unter Last

  • Zahlen- und Datenaffinität. Du arbeitest sicher mit Traffic- und Performance-Metriken und leitest daraus Handlungsempfehlungen ab.

  • Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau, Englisch verhandlungssicher

Nice-to-have

  • Verständnis von Web Performance, Core Web Vitals und dem Google CrUX Report

  • Erfahrung mit HubSpot oder einem vergleichbaren CRM

  • E-Commerce-Hintergrund, idealerweise mit Shopsystemen wie Shopify, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Shopware oder Magento


Warum einsteigen?


  • Wir richten dir deinen Arbeitsplatz ein - vom Bildschirm bis zum Bürostuhl

  • Event-Slots: Mehrmals im Jahr könnt ihr abstimmen, was gemacht wird - wolltest Du nicht schon immer mal mit deinen Kolleg:innen Kart fahren? Vote for it!

  • Speed.Fest: Wir treffen uns jedes Quartal alle gemeinsam in unserem HQ in Hamburg für Workshops, gutes Essen, Events und eine tolle Zeit

  • Persönliches Ausbildungsbudget: Wir helfen Dir, Deine Karriere und Deine Fähigkeiten auszubauen

  • Monatliches, flexibles Benefit Budget: 50€ pro Monat, dass Du frei auf das für Dich passende Benefit verteilen kannst - von ÖPNV über Shopping Gutscheine bis hin zur Gym-Mitgliedschaft

  • Zukunftssichere Altersvorsorge: Bringe deine Altersvorsorge mit oder lass dich von unseren Experten beraten


Countdown

4️⃣… Du teilst deinen Lebenslauf, dein LinkedIn oder Xing-Profil mit uns.

We are looking for a highly structured and proactive Chief of Staff to work closely with our CEO and support the execution of selected strategic and cross-functional initiatives.

You will help translate company priorities into clear projects, responsibilities, and next steps. You will independently own assigned projects end-to-end, prepare strategic decisions, and coordinate initiatives involving different functions and senior stakeholders.   • Maintain a clear view of what the company has committed to and where each commitment stands.


Executive communication and external stakeholders

  • Prepare board materials, investor updates, and decision papers for the CEO and Executive Team, drawing input from relevant stakeholders.
  • Prepare with the CEO ahead of board meetings, partnership discussions, and external engagements, and make sure the follow-ups are picked up.
  • Support investor relations and board processes as they arise.

CEO & Executive Team Support

At OroraTech, you can expect a down-to-earth, yet high-caliber work environment.   • Coordinate across functions: Coordinate with Sales (pipeline), Customer Success (value-delivery), Product (what to sell), and Finance (forecasting) to drive expansion deals

  • Own forecasting and planning: Build accurate expansion forecasts. Coordinate deal timelines. Keep the business informed and on track.

  • Translate roadmap into revenue: Work with Product and Marketing to turn new modules into concrete expansion conversations with the right customers at the right time.

  • Help building the function as it scales: Turn what you learn into reusable process, qualification criteria, pricing guardrails, forecasting templates, rules of engagement with Sales and Customer Value. Where the playbook doesn't exist yet, you help writing it

Your Profile

We're looking for someone who can build, close, and scale. Here's what typically works:

  • 2-4 years in high-performance environments: A proven track record of hitting, and significantly overachieving, quarterly or yearly commercial targets, in account management, sales, or a customer success role with a real commercial component.

  • Proven commercial track record in B2B SaaS companies.

  • Extremely smart and driven – you connect dots quickly, learn fast, and push hard to win

  • Excellent stakeholder management – you navigate complex organizations, build relationships with senior buyers (Heads of Procurement, C-Level), and align internal teams

  • Negotiation toughness – you hold your ground in price discussions without burning bridges

  • Process-oriented – you own details: contracts, terms, renewal dates, forecasting

  • Genuine interest in industrial procurement – you want to understand how manufacturing companies work and speak their language

  • Native German + fluent English

Why This Role is Awesome

This is the first dedicated Account Manager seat at Tacto. Some first structures exist, but most of the function is still yours to build: the quota model, the rules of engagement with Sales and Customer Value, the process itself. Get this right, and expansion becomes Tacto's biggest new revenue lever within two to three years, that's the scale of upside on the table. Do it well for the first 12 to 18 months, and you define your next step: a bigger book of accounts, leading the function as it grows into a full team, or a move into Sales or Customer Value leadership.

What This Role Is - and Isn't

  • This is not customer support with a sales quota bolted on. You'll be measured on revenue, not on being liked, and some weeks that means pushing a commercial conversation the customer wasn't asking for.

  • This is not a mature, handed-to-you playbook. You'll build your own pipeline, your own forecast discipline, and parts of the process itself.

  • Prove you can turn module adoption into signed expansion revenue, and we'll back you owning a bigger book, leading the function, or moving into Sales or CV leadership next.

Why Tacto

  • We bet on young talent and mean it. We consistently back smart, hungry, young people with real ownership early. The large majority of our Leadership Team was promoted internally, you deliver impact and the sky is the limit at Tacto.

  • Backed to win big. We're Sequoia and Index Ventures-funded, with more than €50M raised. We're building Tacto to be the lighthouse for European industrial AI.

  • A truly AI-native organization, with every resource you could dream of. All the leading AI tools and custom agents at your fingertips, plus dedicated people who keep us at the frontier.

  • High bar, high speed, genuinely fun. You'll be surrounded by extremely smart and ambitious people who set the bar high and push you to get better every week. Intense, fast, and the opposite of boring.

  • A front-row seat in the European startup ecosystem. Weekly exposure to leading founders and operators through internal and external events (Lunch & Learns, hackathons, community gatherings). Get a glimpse here: https://luma.com/tacto

  • You'll build something that lasts and that matters. You'll help build the company that keeps European industry competitive for the long term.

Our Background

Tacto is building the intelligence layer that connects AI to the physical world of manufacturing, starting with procurement. AI is transforming every industry, but it stops at the factory gate. The knowledge that holds manufacturing together - part costs, suppliers, materials - is scattered across systems and people. Over 50% of a product's cost originates from suppliers, making procurement the single largest cost lever in manufacturing and the missing connection between the digital and the physical world. Yet it still runs on Excel and legacy systems. We're changing that with our Procurement Intelligence Platform, trusted by hundreds of companies running billions of Euros of material.

Based in Munich, we are 100+ passionate builders who are in-office, with high expectations, fast growth, and a lot of fun. We are supported by >€50m from Sequoia, Index, and Europe's leading tech entrepreneurs and industry veterans.

Why It Matters

Manufacturing forms Europe's economic backbone, driving a fourth of Europe's GDP and providing over 30% of jobs. These hidden champions and global market leaders manufacture the physical world around us, from the machines that build our cities to the medical devices that save lives.

But the world is changing. The US dominates the digital world of bits. China is scaling the world of atoms, manufacturing at unprecedented speed and scale. Geopolitics are more uncertain than ever. Europe's strength lies in its deep industrial knowledge through generations of engineering. Manufacturing worldwide runs on European machines and software. But that heritage is only an advantage if we leverage it in the age of AI.

Tacto builds the AI that connects Atoms and Bits, empowering our Industrial Base to Stay Stronger and building a lighthouse for European tech.

What We Offer

The people at Tacto are passionate about building the organization, growing themselves, and our product while having fun and being real. We have high expectations, great talent density, and a culture where your ambition, performance, and agency are what count - not where you come from or how big your ego is. You'll grow at the forefront of AI, have real ownership and impact, and be surrounded by the best people in their field who challenge you and make you better every day. That is demanding and rewarding, but that's where we thrive. Besides that you have:

  • Money: Competitive salary & equity in the company with real upside, so you are invested in our success

  • Workplace: A vibrant in-office culture (> 4 days/week) in a beautiful office in central Munich

  • Development: A development budget and regular exposure to exceptional people, e.g., Lunch & Learns, peer mentoring, external speakers

  • Time off: 26 + 4 vacation days per year (4 fixed “company rest days”) as well as regular off-sites and team events

  • Health: Wellpass membership, of course, a fruit basket (!), and access to Jobrad, for your health

  • Family & Social Security: Voluntary pension contribution, voluntary KITA subsidy for your children

title: Consultant Corporate Finance & Unternehmensnachfolge (m/w/d) - Teilzeit
description:
Du verbindest analytische Unternehmensbewertung mit einem klaren Blick für die tatsächliche Finanzierbarkeit?

Genau solche Zusammenhänge wollen wir für Menschen verständlich machen, die eine Unternehmensnachfolge vorbereiten, aber selbst keinen M&A-Hintergrund haben. Dafür baust du das Themenfeld Finanzierung, Unternehmensbewertung und M&A in einem neuen bundesweiten Projekt von Grund auf auf. Gemeinsam mit der Projektleitung entwickelst du die fachliche Ausrichtung und entscheidest, wie aus komplexen wirtschaftlichen Fragen verlässliche Informationsangebote entstehen. Dabei arbeitest du eng mit unserer Fördermittelexpertise zusammen und bringst dein Wissen selbst in Workshops und Veranstaltungen ein.

Worum es dabei geht: Jedes Jahr stehen Zehntausende kleine und mittlere Unternehmen in Deutschland vor der Nachfolgefrage. Bleibt sie ungelöst, verschwinden Betriebe, Arbeitsplätze, Wissen und regionale Wertschöpfung. Wir wollen dazu beitragen, dieses Rückgrat der deutschen Wirtschaft zu erhalten und Betriebe mit verständlichen Informationsangeboten und praxisnahen Veranstaltungen dabei unterstützen, Unternehmensnachfolgen erfolgreich vorzubereiten und umzusetzen. Ein besonderer Schwerpunkt liegt auf Unternehmensnachfolgen durch Mitarbeitende – sogenannten Employee Buyouts (EBO) – sowie auf genossenschaftlichen Beteiligungsmodellen.

Über uns: NDF ist die auf Fördermittel spezialisierte Marke der Key Progress Makers Advisory GmbH. Wir arbeiten vor allem mit Startups und innovativen Unternehmen, die neue Produkte, Technologien oder Geschäftsmodelle entwickeln und dafür passende Finanzierungsmöglichkeiten suchen. Wir helfen ihnen, Förderpotenziale zu erkennen und anspruchsvolle Vorhaben so zu strukturieren, dass aus einer Idee ein tragfähiges Projekt werden kann. Diese Erfahrung bringen wir nun in ein eigenes öffentlich gefördertes Projekt rund um das Thema Unternehmensnachfolge ein.

Rahmenbedingungen: Die Stelle umfasst 19,5 Stunden pro Woche. Die Arbeitszeit kann nach Absprache flexibel verteilt werden. Start ist zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt, idealerweise im September 2026.

Aufgaben

  • Du entwickelst Workshops, Informationsangebote und digitale Orientierungshilfen zu Unternehmensbewertung, Finanzierung und M&A bei Unternehmensnachfolgen
  • Du vermittelst komplexe wirtschaftliche und finanzielle Zusammenhänge selbst in Workshops, Veranstaltungen und Fachformaten
  • Du entwickelst verständliche Fallbeispiele zu Unternehmenswert, Kaufpreis, Kapitalbedarf, Liquidität und wirtschaftlicher Tragfähigkeit
  • Du bereitest typische Bewertungsverfahren, Finanzierungsmodelle, Dealstrukturen und Transaktionsphasen praxisnah auf
  • Du entwickelst Inhalte für die Projektwebsite, die digitale Plattform und weitere öffentlich zugängliche Informationsformate
  • Du arbeitest eng mit der Fachverantwortung für Fördermittel zusammen und zeigst, wie öffentliche und private Finanzierungsbausteine grundsätzlich zusammenspielen können

Qualifikation

  • Mindestens 3 Jahre praktische Erfahrung in M&A, Corporate Finance, Unternehmensfinanzierung, Transaction Advisory oder Unternehmensnachfolge
  • Fundierte Erfahrung mit Unternehmensbewertung und Finanzierungsmodellen
  • Sicherer Umgang mit Jahresabschlüssen, BWA, GuV und Bilanz
  • Ein sehr gutes Verständnis von Kapitalbedarf, Liquidität, Kapitaldienstfähigkeit und wirtschaftlicher Tragfähigkeit
  • Erfahrung mit kleinen und/oder mittleren Unternehmen und ein Gespür für die Besonderheiten inhabergeführter Betriebe
  • Die Fähigkeit, komplexe Bewertungs-, Finanzierungs- und Transaktionsfragen verständlich und praxisnah zu vermitteln
  • Erfahrung in der Konzeption und Durchführung von Workshops, Informationsformaten oder fachlichen Veranstaltungen
  • Sehr gutes Deutsch und eine sichere professionelle Kommunikation
  • Eine strukturierte, sorgfältige und eigenständige Arbeitsweise
  • Einen reflektierten Umgang mit digitalen Analysewerkzeugen, Finanzmodellen und KI

Ein bestimmter Studienabschluss ist für uns nicht entscheidend. Uns interessiert, an welchen Transaktionen, Finanzierungen oder Bewertungsprojekten du bereits gearbeitet hast, welche Verantwortung du dabei selbst übernommen hast und wie du zu belastbaren Ergebnissen gekommen bist. Entscheidend ist für uns außerdem, dass du mit Eigeninitiative und echtem Gestaltungswillen an neue Fragestellungen herangehst.

Passende Erfahrungen kannst du beispielsweise aus M&A, Corporate Finance, Transaction Advisory, einer Bank, Beteiligungsgesellschaft oder Nachfolgeberatung mitbringen. Kenntnisse zu Mitarbeiterübernahmen oder genossenschaftlichen Beteiligungsmodellen sind von Vorteil, aber keine Voraussetzung. Wichtig ist, dass du Annahmen nachvollziehbar dokumentierst, wirtschaftliche Risiken klar benennst und auch anspruchsvolle Finanzthemen so vermittelst, dass sie nicht unnötig abschreckend wirken.

Benefits

  • Die Möglichkeit, von Beginn an ein Projekt aktiv mit aufzubauen und mit viel Gestaltungsspielraum eigene Ideen umzusetzen
  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit der Projektleitung und kurze Abstimmungswege
  • Ein interdisziplinäres Team mit Expertise aus Finanzierung, Fördermitteln, Marketing und Veranstaltungsmanagement
  • Mobiles Arbeiten und voraussichtlich 1 bis 2 gemeinsame Bürotage pro Woche in Berlin
  • Gelegentliche bundesweite Reisen für Workshops, Veranstaltungen und Netzwerktreffen
  • Eine Arbeitskultur, in der wir Prioritäten realistisch setzen, Mehrarbeit ausgleichen und Schwierigkeiten früh ansprechen
  • Die Perspektive, auch nach der bewilligten Projektlaufzeit bis zum 30.06.2029 gemeinsam weiterzuarbeiten und zusätzliche fachliche Verantwortung zu übernehmen

Die Rolle passt zu dir, wenn …

… du komplexe wirtschaftliche Zusammenhänge gründlich durchdringst und anschließend so erklärst, dass auch Menschen ohne M&A- oder Finanzierungserfahrung sie verstehen.

… du Freude daran hast, Unternehmen mit deinem Wissen zu tragfähigen Entscheidungen und wirtschaftlichem Erfolg zu verhelfen.

… du dir eine moderne, wertschätzende Zusammenarbeit wünschst und deine fachliche Arbeit gerne für ein Projekt einsetzt, dessen gesellschaftlicher und wirtschaftlicher Nutzen unmittelbar erkennbar ist.

So bewirbst du dich

Schick uns zunächst deinen Lebenslauf. Wenn dein Profil zu uns passt, laden wir dich zu einem ersten Kennenlerngespräch ein. Darauf folgt ein fachlicher Austausch; bei Bedarf ergänzen wir den Prozess um eine kurze und klar abgegrenzte Praxisaufgabe. Nach jedem Schritt erhältst du innerhalb weniger Arbeitstage eine Rückmeldung.

Geplanter Start: zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt, idealerweise im September 2026.

Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen unabhängig von Geschlecht und geschlechtlicher Identität, ethnischer oder sozialer Herkunft, Nationalität, Religion oder Weltanschauung, Behinderung, Alter oder sexueller Identität. Entscheidend sind deine Kompetenz, deine Motivation und die Perspektive, die du in das Projekt einbringst.

title: Kaufmännische Projektkoordinator - Fördermittel & Finanzen (m/w/d) I Teilzeit
description:
Du findest Fehler im Budget schneller als andere ihre Schlüssel?

Genau dieses Talent brauchen wir, damit unser neues Förderprojekt im Bereich Unternehmensnachfolge auch administrativ und finanziell auf einem sicheren Fundament steht. Du baust die Projektadministration von Grund auf auf, behältst Budgets und Fristen im Blick und sorgst dafür, dass alle relevanten Unterlagen vollständig sowie jederzeit nachvollziehbar vorliegen. Dabei arbeitest du direkt mit der Projektleitung zusammen und erkennst frühzeitig, wenn Handlungsbedarf besteht.

Worum es dabei geht: Jedes Jahr stehen Zehntausende kleine und mittlere Unternehmen in Deutschland vor der Nachfolgefrage. Bleibt sie ungelöst, verschwinden Betriebe, Arbeitsplätze, Wissen und regionale Wertschöpfung. Wir wollen dazu beitragen, dieses Rückgrat der deutschen Wirtschaft zu erhalten und Betriebe mit verständlichen Informationsangeboten und praxisnahen Veranstaltungen dabei unterstützen, Unternehmensnachfolgen erfolgreich vorzubereiten und umzusetzen.

Über uns: NDF ist die auf Fördermittel spezialisierte Marke der Key Progress Makers Advisory GmbH. Wir arbeiten vor allem mit Startups und innovativen Unternehmen, die neue Produkte, Technologien oder Geschäftsmodelle entwickeln und dafür passende Finanzierungsmöglichkeiten suchen. Wir helfen ihnen, Förderpotenziale zu erkennen und anspruchsvolle Vorhaben so zu strukturieren, dass aus einer Idee ein tragfähiges Projekt werden kann. Diese Erfahrung bringen wir nun in ein eigenes öffentlich gefördertes Projekt rund um das Thema Unternehmensnachfolge ein.

Rahmenbedingungen: Die Stelle umfasst 19,5 Stunden pro Woche. Die Arbeitszeit kann nach Absprache flexibel verteilt werden. Du arbeitest überwiegend mobil und nimmst gelegentlich an gemeinsamen Terminen in Berlin teil. Start ist zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt, idealerweise im September 2026.

Aufgaben

Dein Schwerpunkt liegt auf der Fördermitteladministration, der finanziellen Projektdokumentation und dem Aufbau einer prüfungssicheren digitalen Projektakte. Bei buchhalterischen und personaladministrativen Vorgängen konzentrierst du dich auf die für das Projekt relevanten Unterlagen und arbeitest eng mit der Geschäftsführung, der Projektleitung und unserer externen Steuerberatung zusammen.

  • Du baust eine vollständige digitale Projektakte auf und sorgst dafür, dass Fristen, Nachweise und Unterlagen jederzeit nachvollziehbar dokumentiert sind
  • Du bereitest Mittelanforderungen, Berichte, Änderungsunterlagen und Verwendungsnachweise für das Förderprojekt administrativ vor
  • Du überwachst das Projektbudget, pflegst Kostenstellen und Kontierungen, erstellst regelmäßige Soll-Ist-Auswertungen und bereitest buchhaltungs- und abrechnungsrelevante Unterlagen vor
  • Du stellst sicher, dass Teilnehmendenlisten, Einwilligungen, Veranstaltungsnachweise und abrechnungsrelevante Daten vollständig vorliegen
  • Ergänzend unterstützt du bei der Verwaltung projektbezogener Personalunterlagen, Verträge, Rechnungen, Teilnahmegebühren und offener Forderungen und weist frühzeitig auf Abweichungen oder Risiken hin
  • Du entwickelst klare Vorlagen, Checklisten und digitale Prozesse, damit wiederkehrende administrative Aufgaben zuverlässig und effizient ablaufen

Qualifikation

  • Mindestens drei Jahre praktische Erfahrung in kaufmännischer Verwaltung, Buchhaltung, Projektadministration oder Fördermittelmanagement
  • Sichere Kenntnisse in Buchhaltung, Rechnungsprüfung, Belegzuordnung und Kostenkontierung
  • Erfahrung mit Fristen-, Dokumenten- und Nachweismanagement
  • Sehr gute Kenntnisse in Excel oder einer vergleichbaren Tabellenkalkulation
  • Die Fähigkeit, finanzielle und administrative Unstimmigkeiten frühzeitig zu erkennen und strukturiert aufzuklären
  • Eine sehr sorgfältige, zuverlässige und eigenständige Arbeitsweise
  • Sehr gutes schriftliches Deutsch und eine klare, verbindliche Kommunikation
  • Einen sicheren und diskreten Umgang mit vertraulichen Personal-, Finanz- und Teilnehmendendaten
  • Die Bereitschaft, dich gründlich in Förderbedingungen und digitale Fördersysteme einzuarbeiten
  • Einen reflektierten und datenschutzkonformen Umgang mit digitalen Werkzeugen, Automatisierung und KI

Ein bestimmter Ausbildungs- oder Studienabschluss ist für uns nicht entscheidend. Passende Erfahrungen kannst du beispielsweise aus der kaufmännischen Verwaltung, Buchhaltung, Steuerberatung, Personaladministration oder der Verwaltung öffentlich geförderter Projekte mitbringen.

Wichtig ist, dass du Vorgänge vollständig zu Ende führst, fehlende Informationen verbindlich nachhältst und Risiken nicht nur meldest, sondern bereits mit einem konkreten Lösungsvorschlag aufbereitest.

Benefits

  • Eine verantwortungsvolle Rolle in einem neu entstehenden Projekt mit erkennbarem gesellschaftlichem und wirtschaftlichem Nutzen
  • Viel Gestaltungsspielraum beim Aufbau der Projektadministration und verlässlicher digitaler Prozesse
  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit der Projektleitung, kurze Abstimmungswege und die Möglichkeit, Risiken frühzeitig in Entscheidungen einzubringen
  • Ein flexibles Teilzeitmodell mit überwiegend mobilem Arbeiten und gelegentlichen gemeinsamen Terminen in Berlin
  • Eine moderne und wertschätzende Zusammenarbeit, in der Verbindlichkeit, Eigenverantwortung und sorgfältige Arbeit tatsächlich geschätzt werden
  • Die Perspektive, auch nach der dreijährigen Projektlaufzeit gemeinsam weiterzuarbeiten und mit den aufgebauten Strukturen zusätzliche fachliche Verantwortung für andere Projekte zu übernehmen

Die Rolle passt zu dir, wenn …

… du bei Zahlen, Fristen und Dokumenten genau hinschaust und gerne dafür sorgst, dass auch komplexe Vorgänge sauber strukturiert und jederzeit nachvollziehbar sind.

… du vorausschauend, verbindlich und freundlich beharrlich bist, fehlende Zuarbeiten konsequent einholst und auch unter Zeitdruck ruhig den Überblick behältst.

… du dir eine moderne, wertschätzende Zusammenarbeit wünschst und deine Sorgfalt für ein Projekt einsetzen möchtest, dessen gesellschaftlicher und wirtschaftlicher Nutzen unmittelbar erkennbar ist.

So bewirbst du dich

Schick uns zunächst deinen Lebenslauf. Wenn dein Profil zu uns passt, laden wir dich zu einem ersten Kennenlerngespräch ein. Darauf folgt ein fachlicher Austausch; bei Bedarf ergänzen wir den Prozess um eine kurze und klar abgegrenzte Praxis- oder Excel-Aufgabe. Nach jedem Schritt erhältst du innerhalb weniger Arbeitstage eine Rückmeldung.

Geplanter Start: idealerweise 01.09.2026.

Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen unabhängig von Geschlecht und geschlechtlicher Identität, ethnischer oder sozialer Herkunft, Nationalität, Religion oder Weltanschauung, Behinderung, Alter oder sexueller Identität. Entscheidend sind deine Kompetenz, deine Motivation und die Perspektive, die du in das Projekt einbringst.

Wir arbeiten vor allem mit Startups und innovativen Unternehmen, die neue Produkte, Technologien oder Geschäftsmodelle entwickeln und dafür passende Finanzierungsmöglichkeiten suchen.   • Erfahrung mit Förderangeboten für kleine und mittlere Unternehmen, etwa in den Bereichen Innovation, Digitalisierung, Investitionen, Transformation, Energieeffizienz oder Unternehmensnachfolge

title: Founding Product Engineer
description:
About the Role

This is a founding engineering hire at an early-stage, AI-powered platform built for industrial energy procurement and cost optimisation. You'll join a small, high-conviction team and take genuine ownership — from shaping the architecture to shipping features directly with customers. The platform handles real-time energy market data, forecasting, portfolio management, and optimisation at enterprise scale.

If you're a generalist engineer with a strong product mindset, comfort with ambiguity, and a curiosity for data-intensive domains, this role is a rare opportunity to have outsized impact from day one.

Note: Visa sponsorship is not available for this role.

What You'll Do

  • Own the full product lifecycle — from design and requirements through to deployment and iteration.

  • Translate product objectives into clear, actionable requirements in close collaboration with customers.

  • Design simple, iterative solutions to complex energy procurement and market problems.

  • Build performant backend services for a highly data-intensive application.

  • Develop intuitive, elegant user interfaces for a sophisticated decision-support system.

  • Train time-series forecasting models for power consumption and renewables production.

  • Develop and refine linear optimisation algorithms to reduce customer energy costs.

  • Help define and evolve the core tech stack — including PostgreSQL, TypeScript, React, and Python.

What We're Looking For

Must-haves:

  • 2+ years of software engineering experience delivering scalable web applications in an early-stage startup environment.

  • Proven track record of delivering full product features independently, working directly with customers.

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals — you write robust, maintainable, scalable code.

  • Hands-on experience building backend services for data-intensive applications.

  • Experience building frontend UIs for complex, data-rich decision-support tools.

  • A genuine product mindset: you think about outcomes, not just outputs.

  • Comfort thriving in a fast-paced, early-stage environment with high ambiguity and rapid change.

Strong advantages:

  • Experience with time-series forecasting and/or linear optimisation.

  • Familiarity with PostgreSQL, React, Python; exposure to FastAPI, TypeScript, or Supabase is a plus.

  • Background as a CTO, founding engineer, or startup founder.

  • Corporate background (e.g. industrials, energy, consulting) paired with a demonstrated startup mindset and grit.

  • Curiosity for energy markets, industrial technology, or data-intensive B2B applications.

Location

This role is based in Munich, Germany. You'll work on-site the majority of the week, with flexibility for occasional remote days. Fully remote arrangements are not available for this position.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Salary: €85,000 – €140,000 per year, depending on experience.

  • Meaningful early-stage equity participation.

  • Direct influence over product direction, tech stack, and company culture.

  • A lean, high-calibre team working on a complex, high-stakes problem in the European energy transition.

title: Founding Enterprise Account Executive
description:
About the Role

A fast-growing, early-stage B2B SaaS company building an AI-native pricing optimization platform is looking for a Founding Enterprise Account Executive to own and scale enterprise sales from the ground up. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with the founding team to define GTM strategy, build repeatable playbooks, and land high-ACV enterprise customers — deals that will directly shape both product direction and commercial trajectory.

This is a rare opportunity to be the first enterprise sales hire at a company with a differentiated product in a high-value, underserved category. If you thrive in ambiguity, love building, and want your fingerprints on every aspect of a growing sales org, this role is for you.

What You'll Do

  • Own the full enterprise sales cycle — from self-sourced prospecting through discovery, negotiation, and close.

  • Run consultative discovery with senior economic buyers including CFOs, CROs, CPOs, and Heads of Monetization.

  • Carry and accurately forecast an ambitious revenue target while maintaining week-to-week pipeline health.

  • Design, document, and iterate the enterprise playbook covering outreach, qualification, deal structure, commercial terms, and close mechanics.

  • Partner directly with founders on GTM strategy, ICP refinement, and positioning — feeding market insight back into product and sales.

  • Establish CRM discipline and operating rhythms for pipeline hygiene, prioritization, and clean forecasting.

  • Sell AI-natively by leveraging and improving AI agents and workflows to automate repeatable buyer-journey tasks, reserving human judgment for key deal moments.

  • Act as a trusted advisor to customers and deliver actionable feedback to product and engineering from live deals.

  • In your first 90 days: learn the product and ICP deeply, build pipeline through outbound and inbound, close initial deals end-to-end, and begin codifying a repeatable playbook.

What We're Looking For

Required:

  • 5–8+ years of enterprise B2B tech sales experience with a proven track record of closing high-ACV deals end-to-end.

  • Demonstrated success self-sourcing pipeline and consistently carrying and exceeding revenue targets.

  • Strong experience running multi-stakeholder enterprise deals and building consensus up to the C-suite.

  • Proficiency with CRM and sales-engagement tooling (e.g., Salesforce, Gong) and experience building automations for repeatable sales tasks.

  • Comfort working with AI-driven workflows and directing AI tools in a sales context.

  • Strategic, analytical approach to market assessment paired with creative, tactical execution.

  • High tolerance for ambiguity and ability to thrive in a fast-paced startup environment.

  • Professional fluency in English.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with pricing, monetization, CPQ, or billing solutions.

  • Background at a high-growth B2B SaaS or AI startup in a founding or early sales role.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Salary: $200,000 – $250,000 USD annually (on-target or base; please confirm with hiring team)

  • Early-stage equity opportunity

  • High-impact, high-ownership founding role with direct founder access

Note: Visa sponsorship is not available for this role.

Location

This is an on-site role based in Amsterdam, Netherlands. Candidates should be prepared to work from the Amsterdam office.

title: Senior Robotic Systems Engineer
description:
About the Role

This is a foundational senior engineering hire at an early-stage industrial robotics startup in Munich. You will own the core robotics software stack end-to-end — from motion planning and control through to real-world deployment of an intelligent robotic work cell built for the hardest manual tasks in industry: surface finishing, welding, and coating.

This is a high-ownership, hands-on role for someone who thrives on turning real hardware into reliable, production-grade systems. You'll shape architecture decisions from day one on a small, ambitious team pushing the boundaries of industrial automation.

What You'll Do

  • Own and evolve the core robotics software stack of the work cell

  • Develop and optimize motion planning, trajectory generation, and control algorithms for industrial robot arms

  • Integrate perception systems — cameras, force/torque sensors, LiDAR — into real-time control loops

  • Implement industrial safety concepts and fail-safe behaviors

  • Lead on-site testing, calibration, and commissioning activities

  • Drive system architecture decisions and establish engineering best practices

What We're Looking For

Required:

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in robotics engineering, with a strong focus on real-world hardware (simulation-only backgrounds are not a fit)

  • Demonstrated experience with motion planning and trajectory generation for industrial robot arms in production environments (e.g. KUKA, ABB, Fanuc, Universal Robots)

  • Proficiency in C++ and/or Python

  • Experience with ROS 2

  • Hands-on integration of force/torque sensors and/or vision systems

  • Solid grounding in kinematics, dynamics, and control theory

  • Eligible to work in Germany — visa sponsorship is not available

Nice to Have:

  • Background in surface finishing, welding, or industrial coating applications

  • Experience with 3D CAD tools (SolidWorks, CATIA)

  • Familiarity with industrial communication protocols such as EtherCAT or OPC-UA

  • German language skills (not required)

Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive cash salary in the range of €75,000 – €110,000 annually

  • Meaningful equity participation — ownership is a core part of the offer

Location

  • Munich, Bavaria, Germany — fully on-site

  • Remote work is not available for this role

  • Candidates must already be eligible to work in Germany; no visa sponsorship is offered

title: Senior Systems Engineer

description:
As Senior Product Manager in the Regulatory Group at Flinn, you'll be owning a product at a major inflection point. It has a deep data foundation, a task-based workflow that saves regulatory experts time, and a growing base of enterprise customers. Your job is to take our regulatory product from early traction to enterprise-ready: benchmarking what's working, closing workflow gaps that matter to highly specialized users, and finding the improvement vectors that could change how regulatory teams work. The path there is earned through sharp prioritization, close customer proximity, and the ability to turn complex problems into concrete steps.

Why Flinn?

  • Make a Meaningful Impact: Your work at Flinn contributes directly to solutions that improve people’s health and lives by making high-quality health products accessible for everyone.

  • Experienced, well-funded, highly professional: As well-funded startup veterans, we know how to sustain long-term business health and success, ensuring an environment for continuous personal growth.

What’s in it for you?

  • Join a fast-growing, well-funded European startup backed by experienced founders and investors.

  • Be part of a mission-driven health-tech company whose work directly improves people’s lives.

  • Take end-to-end ownership of core operational processes that keep the company running.

  • Play a key role in scaling Flinn, shaping how operations work as we grow.

  • Work in a high-trust, low-ego environment with autonomy and clear ownership.

  • Enjoy flexible working hours, remote flexibility, and regular team time in Vienna.

  • Work in a net-zero company where all unavoidable CO₂ emissions are compensated with carefully selected, high-quality removal certificates.

  • Receive one of the most employee-friendly equity packages, including fair vesting terms and profit-sharing opportunities.

  • Grow in a professional, high-standard environment that supports long-term personal and career development.

Your contributions to our journey:

  • Own the Regulatory product roadmap and take the product to one that enterprise customers genuinely rely on at scale.

  • Stay close to customers. Understand the day-to-day workflow of regulatory experts well enough to know which friction points are worth solving and which are noise.

  • Identify and prioritize incremental improvements that reduce real workflow friction, while keeping a longer view on where the product could create entirely new ways of working for your users.

  • Work tightly with engineering and customer success to move ideas from discovery to shipped and adopted

What you need to be successful:

  • Experience building complex products from the ground up

  • Strong ability and openness to operate at both strategic and execution levels, and to switch between them effortlessly.

  • High curiosity and hands-on interest in AI-first products.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset, resilience under pressure, a strong sense of ownership, and a bias toward action and learning.

  • Excellent communication skills (fluent in verbal and written English; German is a plus).

Attributes we are looking for:

  • 3+ years of experience in Product Management.

  • Proven experience taking a B2B product from early traction to scaled adoption.

  • Experience working on workflow-heavy or domain-specialist tools (regulatory, legal, compliance, finance).

  • Demonstrable ability to break complex problems into structured, executable steps.

  • Strong personal organization skills enabling you to own your workload without a need for process scaffolding.

  • Comfortable working in ambiguity with limited resourcing.

  • Hands-on experience with AI-first or AI-enabled products is a strong plus.

  • Experience working in both small startups and larger scale-ups is a bonus.

  • Prior background in business, strategy, or consulting before moving into product management is a strong plus. Industry experience in medtech or pharma is a nice-to-have, not a requirement.

Kurze Wege, ehrliches Feedback, keine politischen Spielchen. Keine Hierarchie-Ebenen zwischen dir und den Leuten, die Entscheidungen treffen.

Deine Aufgaben

Du arbeitest in Kundenprojekten bei großen Unternehmen und öffentlichen Auftraggebern, eingebettet in deren Teams, mit voller Verantwortung für deinen Bereich.

  • Konzeption, Entwicklung und Test von Microservices im Java-Umfeld
  • API-Entwicklung: REST und SOAP, synchron und asynchron, Spezifikation mit OpenAPI 3
  • Prozessautomatisierung mit Camunda BPM
  • Testautomatisierung mit JUnit 5 und Cucumber
  • Betrieb der eigenen Services: Deployment, Monitoring, Fehleranalyse
  • Architektur mitgestalten, nicht nur umsetzen
  • Code generieren, reviewen und refactoren mit Claude Code, Copilot oder Cursor
  • Abstimmung mit Schnittstellenpartnern über Teamgrenzen hinweg

Die meisten kommen ein bis zwei Tage die Woche in eins der Büros. Zwang ist das aber keiner. Beim Kunden vor Ort bist du nur für einzelne Termine alle paar Wochen.

Ehrlich vorab: Rufbereitschaft gehört dazu

In einem Teil dieser Projekte betreust du die Services, die du entwickelst, auch im Betrieb — inklusive turnusmäßiger Rufbereitschaft. Das ist geregelt und wird im Team geteilt.

Wo du landest

Je nach Projekt und deiner Erfahrung:

  • Großkonzerne wie Deutsche Bahn / DB Systel (eisenbahnspezifische Domänen: Fahrplanmanagement, Vertrieb, Leit- und Sicherungstechnik)
  • Öffentlicher Sektor / Behörden (z. B. Bundesagentur für Arbeit, ITZBund, Bundesdruckerei) – regulierte Umgebungen, Barrierefreiheit, Security by Design
  • Enterprise- und Mittelstands-Kunden aus verschiedensten Branchen

Erfahrung in einem dieser Umfelder ist ein starkes Plus – sag uns in den Fragen, wo du herkommst.

Was du mitbringst

Senior-Level. Unsere Kunden brauchen Leute, die ab Tag eins liefern und eigenständig arbeiten.

Backend-Kern (das erwarten wir):

  • Java und Spring Boot, dazu Spring Data und Hibernate/JPA
  • Microservices: Konzeption, Entwicklung, Test
  • REST- und SOAP-Webservices (JSON/XML über HTTP), OpenAPI 3
  • PostgreSQL und Oracle
  • JUnit 5 und Cucumber
  • Docker und Kubernetes
  • CI/CD mit GitLab Pipelines, Build mit Maven
  • Git, Jira, Confluence, agiles Arbeiten

Das unterscheidet dich:

  • Camunda BPM aus echten Projekten, nicht aus einem Tutorial
  • OAuth 2.0 und Keycloak für Authentifizierung und Autorisierung

Von Vorteil (kein Muss):

  • Apache Kafka und asynchrone Kommunikation
  • XML, XSD, XSLT
  • Erfahrung in komplexen Projekten mit mehreren beteiligten Teams
  • J2EE-Altbestand und dessen Migration nach Spring Boot

Sprache: Deutsch als Muttersprache oder auf C1-/C2-Niveau, Englisch fließend. Du stimmst dich täglich mit Fachbereichen und Schnittstellenpartnern ab.

Du musst nicht alles können. Wichtig ist der Java-Kern und dass du dich schnell in neue Stacks reinfindest.

AI-Tools sind Pflicht, kein Bonus

Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor: Damit musst du produktiv arbeiten können. Nicht weil wir hip sein wollen, sondern weil unsere Kunden das erwarten und wir auch so arbeiten. Wenn du AI-Tools für einen Hype hältst und lieber alles selbst tippst: falsche Firma. Intern investieren wir in deine AI-Skills.

Was wir bieten

  • Homeoffice, Büro oder Mix, du entscheidest
  • MacBook (außer der Kunde stellt eigene Hardware)
  • Verschiedene Kunden, verschiedene Projekte
  • Die Gründer sind deine direkten Ansprechpartner
  • Internes Upskilling in AI-Entwicklung

Bewerbung

Lebenslauf reicht. Kein Anschreiben nötig. Nach einer kurzen Video-Frage-Runde (2×90 Sekunden) melden wir uns innerhalb weniger Tage.

title: Senior AI-Native Fullstack Engineer (m/w/d)
description:
Job description

We are building modern, customer-facing software for the temp-staffing industry, integrating capabilities from multiple ERP systems and countries into reliable applications, workflows, services, and reusable platform components.

We are looking for a product-minded senior fullstack engineer who can turn ambiguous business requirements and complex existing systems into production-grade backend services, APIs, integrations, internal tools, and intuitive user interfaces.

TypeScript is central to our technology landscape. Experience with .NET and C# is strongly valued, while engineers with a background in strongly typed languages such as Java are also welcome. Comfort working across different stacks and languages is essential.

AI and LLM tooling are central to how we work. You should use AI-native workflows to explore faster, build in parallel, validate assumptions, and ship high-quality production solutions. You should care about correctness and maintainability, understand integration and business edge cases, choose simple and robust solutions, and own outcomes from exploration to production.


Your tasks

  • Fullstack Product Engineering: Build customer-facing applications, backend services, APIs, internal tools, admin interfaces, automation, job runners, and configurable workflows
  • Backend & Domain Logic: Design maintainable services, APIs, business logic, asynchronous processes, validation rules, and reusable components
  • Frontend Engineering: Build intuitive and maintainable user interfaces using TypeScript and modern frontend frameworks
  • Integrations: Connect applications with ERP systems, internal platforms, external APIs, databases, queues, files, and third-party services
  • Cloud & Production Ownership: Deploy and operate reliable cloud solutions, preferably AWS, owning monitoring, alerts, failure handling, security, performance, cost, and operational reliability


Your profile

  • Hands-on with Claude Code, Codex, and agent-based workflows; GitHub Copilot-style autocomplete alone is not enough
  • Familiar with worktrees, subagents, MCP, structured prompts, harness engineering, parallelization, and validating AI-generated code and analysis to production quality
  • Strong fullstack/backend experience, ideally with .NET and TypeScript
  • Able to build production-grade services, APIs, scripts, tools, automation, and clean interfaces; comfortable with version control, review, debugging, testing, and existing systems
  • Strong understanding of application architecture, API design, domain modeling, integration patterns, asynchronous processing, and maintainable software boundaries
  • Comfortable with SQL, relational databases, schema design, transactions, migrations, indexing, and application-level data access
  • Hands-on with AWS or similar cloud environments, including storage, databases, queues, containers, serverless/scheduled processing, SDKs, and APIs
  • Understands deployment, secrets, networking, permissions, runtime configuration, scalability, performance, cost, and operational trade-offs
You may be a good fit if you are driven to improve how software is built, use AI and agent-based workflows to move faster, experiment with better approaches, and turn ambiguous problems into reliable production solutions. You should enjoy working across the stack, taking ownership beyond predefined tickets, improving existing systems, and rigorously validating AI-generated output rather than accepting it at face value. This role is less suitable for someone who prefers narrow responsibilities, fixed processes, or working within a single technical area without contributing to broader product and engineering outcomes.


Your benefits

  • Work across AI-powered SaaS and cloud-native products, use modern AI tooling daily, and shape pragmatic infrastructure that helps teams ship faster and more safely
  • Collaboration in an empathetic, appreciative team with room to contribute ideas and take ownership
  • Individual development opportunities, structured onboarding, and interdisciplinary collaboration
  • Flexible working models including hybrid work, home office, and mobile working
  • A modern tech environment and agile ways of working
  • Additional benefits such as pension plans, health offers, and employee discounts
